title: 17s and Up-and-Down Conditioning
description: Players sprint the width of the court 17 times within a time limit, then run full-court up-and-downs, a staple basketball conditioning combination.

content.objective: Complete a demanding width-of-court sprint count within a set time to build game-level conditioning.
content.setup: Players line up on the sideline with the full width of the court open to sprint.
instructions: Sprint width-to-width across the court, counting each crossing as one.
Complete 17 total crossings within the set time limit (commonly 60 seconds for older groups).
Rest for the planned interval, then run one or two full-court up-and-down sprints.
Repeat the full combination for the planned number of sets.
coachingPoints: Keep a consistent pace rather than sprinting hard early and fading late.
Touch each sideline clearly before turning back.
Push through the final few crossings rather than coasting to the buzzer.
commonMistakes: Cutting the turn short instead of touching the sideline.
Starting too fast and being unable to maintain the pace.
Losing count under fatigue and finishing short of the real total.
content.safety: Build up to this conditioning level gradually; stop if a player shows signs of overheating or distress.
